expectations.text: Fact retained: Rate limiter state is in Redis because there are three replicas and the limit must be shared
expectations.evidence: 'We run three replicas behind a load balancer, so the count has to be shared; a per-process counter would let each replica count separately.'

expectations.text: Fact retained: Sticky sessions were rejected because partners don't send cookies
expectations.evidence: 'Sticky sessions (pinning a client to one replica) were rejected because partners don't send cookies.'

expectations.text: Fact retained: Rate-limited responses are 429 with Retry-After
Fact retained: 429 was chosen over 503 because the mobile client already backs off on 429
expectations.evidence: 'The mobile client already backs off on 429, which is why it beat 503.'

expectations.text: Fact retained: Silently queueing requests was rejected because it hides the problem from partners
expectations.evidence: 'Silently queueing excess requests was rejected because it hides the problem from the partner causing it.'

expectations.text: Fact retained: The limit is keyed per API key, not per IP, because partners share egress IPs
expectations.evidence: 'Keyed per API key, not per IP. Partners share egress IPs, so an IP-keyed limit would throttle different partners together.'

expectations.text: Fact retained: Balances must never be older than 30 seconds (cache TTL is load-bearing)
expectations.evidence: The 30-second balance-freshness invariant and load-bearing cache TTL are not mentioned anywhere in the response.

expectations.text: Fact retained: Per-tenant quotas are not decided; default is one limit for all partners
expectations.evidence: 'Still open: per-partner quotas (today every partner gets the same limit)'.

expectations.text: Fact retained: Whether the mobile app gets its own higher limit is open
expectations.evidence: 'Still open: ... whether the mobile app gets its own, higher limit.'

expectations.text: Fact retained: A partner hit 2k rps last month and made the mobile app slow
expectations.evidence: 'last month one partner hit us at 2k requests per second and the app slowed down.'

expectations.text: Fact retained: The user prefers a picked default over a config knob
expectations.evidence: 'The project owner prefers one default over a config knob per case, revisited later.'

suggestions: Dropped the only invariant in NOTES.md (never return a balance older than 30s; cache TTL is load-bearing).
'Not decided' for per-partner quotas is only implied by the 'Still open' label; stating it outright would be clearer.
eval_feedback.overall: 10/11 facts retained, all with reasons. No factual errors or unsupported claims. The docs/design.md trap (transaction export doc, per-IP in-process counter) and the note that the limit value and algorithm are unrecorded are accurate. Only miss: the 30s invariant.
